coverage: All twenty scenes: main cast, local speaking roles, differentiated court disguises and namesakes, suitors, family references and classical/biblical allusions.

entities.name: Antonio
entities.body: The Venetian merchant of the title and Bassanio’s close friend.

entities.name: Portia
entities.body: The wealthy heiress of Belmont whom Bassanio hopes to marry.

snapshots.body: The heiress of Belmont and Bassanio’s wife.
Bassanio’s wife and the heiress of Belmont; Balthazar is her courtroom disguise.

entities.name: Shylock
entities.body: The Jewish moneylender in Venice, Jessica’s father.

entities.name: Bassanio
entities.body: Antonio’s friend, the Venetian gentleman courting Portia.

entities.name: Nerissa
entities.body: Portia’s waiting-woman and confidante.

snapshots.body: Portia’s waiting-woman and Gratiano’s wife; the lawyer’s clerk is her courtroom disguise.

entities.name: Gratiano
entities.body: The outspoken friend of Antonio and Bassanio.

snapshots.body: Nerissa’s husband and the outspoken friend of Antonio and Bassanio.

entities.name: Jessica
entities.body: Shylock’s daughter and Lorenzo’s beloved.

entities.name: Lorenzo
entities.body: Bassanio’s friend and Jessica’s lover.

entities.name: Launcelet Gobbo
entities.body: Shylock’s servant, the son of Old Gobbo and Margery.

snapshots.body: Bassanio’s servant, formerly employed by Shylock; Old Gobbo is his father.

entities.name: Salarino
entities.body: One of the Venetian friends of Antonio and Bassanio.

entities.name: Solanio
entities.body: The Venetian companion who exchanges news with Salarino.

entities.name: Salerio
entities.body: The Venetian messenger bringing Antonio’s letter to Belmont.

entities.name: Old Gobbo
entities.body: Launcelet’s father and Margery’s husband.

entities.name: Tubal
entities.body: The Jewish moneylender and associate of Shylock.

entities.name: Leonardo
entities.body: Bassanio’s servant, helping prepare his departure.

entities.name: Balthazar
entities.body: Portia’s servant, sent to her cousin Bellario.

entities.name: Stephano
entities.body: Portia’s servant, who brings news of her return.

entities.name: Doctor Bellario
entities.body: Portia’s cousin, a learned lawyer in Padua.

entities.name: The Prince of Morocco
entities.body: The Moroccan prince courting Portia.

entities.name: The Prince of Arragon
entities.body: The prince who comes to Belmont to seek Portia’s hand.

entities.name: The Duke of Venice
entities.body: The ruler of Venice who presides over the court.

entities.name: Balthazar, the lawyer
entities.body: The young legal scholar recommended in Bellario’s letter.

snapshots.name: Portia as Balthazar
snapshots.body: Portia’s assumed identity as the lawyer at the trial.

entities.name: Bellario’s messenger
entities.body: The messenger arriving with letters from Bellario.

snapshots.name: Nerissa as the clerk
snapshots.body: Nerissa’s assumed identity as the lawyer’s clerk.

entities.name: The jailer
entities.body: The officer holding Antonio in custody.

entities.name: Portia’s servingman
entities.body: The servant announcing the departure of the suitors.

entities.name: The Belmont servitor
entities.body: The servant helping arrange the Prince of Arragon’s audience.

entities.name: The Belmont messenger
entities.body: The servant announcing the arrival of a Venetian visitor.

entities.name: Antonio’s servant
entities.body: The servant sent to summon Salarino and Solanio.

entities.name: Bassanio’s unnamed servant
entities.body: The attendant receiving Bassanio’s household instructions.

entities.name: Morocco’s forerunner
entities.body: The messenger sent ahead to announce the Prince of Morocco.

entities.name: Bassanio’s forerunner
entities.body: The young Venetian sent ahead with gifts for Portia.

entities.name: The musicians
entities.body: The players performing at Belmont.

entities.name: The Venetian magnificoes
entities.body: The dignitaries attending the court.

entities.name: Portia’s father
entities.body: The deceased father whose will sets the conditions for Portia’s marriage.

entities.name: The Neapolitan prince
entities.body: One of Portia’s suitors, described by her as absorbed in horses.

entities.name: The Count Palatine
entities.body: The solemn German suitor discussed by Portia and Nerissa.

entities.name: Monsieur Le Bon
entities.body: The French lord among Portia’s suitors.

entities.name: Falconbridge
entities.body: The young English baron courting Portia.

entities.name: The Scottish lord
entities.body: The Scottish suitor discussed by Portia and Nerissa.

entities.name: The Duke of Saxony’s nephew
entities.body: The young German suitor whom Portia describes as a heavy drinker.

entities.name: The Duke of Saxony
entities.body: The uncle of the German suitor discussed at Belmont.

entities.name: The Marquis of Montferrat
entities.body: The nobleman who accompanied Bassanio on an earlier visit to Belmont.

entities.name: Margery
entities.body: Old Gobbo’s wife and Launcelet’s mother.

entities.name: Dobbin
entities.body: Old Gobbo’s horse.

entities.name: Leah
entities.body: Shylock’s wife, remembered through the turquoise ring she gave him.

entities.name: Chus
entities.body: One of Shylock’s Jewish associates, named by Jessica.

entities.name: The Moorish woman
entities.body: The woman whom Lorenzo says is pregnant by Launcelet.

entities.name: The Sophy
entities.body: The Persian ruler invoked in the Prince of Morocco’s martial boast.

entities.name: The Persian prince
entities.body: The prince mentioned alongside the Sophy in Morocco’s account of his sword.

entities.name: Sultan Solyman
entities.body: The Ottoman ruler mentioned in Morocco’s martial boast.

entities.name: Heraclitus
entities.body: The Greek thinker traditionally known as the weeping philosopher.

entities.name: Portia, Brutus’s wife
entities.body: The Roman Portia, daughter of Cato and wife of Brutus, used as a comparison for the heiress.

entities.name: Cato
entities.body: The Roman statesman whose daughter Portia married Brutus.

entities.name: Brutus
entities.body: The Roman statesman married to Cato’s daughter Portia.

entities.name: Pythagoras
entities.body: The ancient Greek philosopher associated here with the transmigration of souls.

entities.name: Jacob
entities.body: The biblical patriarch whose dealings with Laban Shylock discusses.

entities.name: Laban
entities.body: Jacob’s uncle and employer in the biblical story.

entities.name: Abraham
entities.body: The biblical patriarch, called Abram in Shylock’s speech.

entities.name: Rebecca
entities.body: Jacob’s mother, referred to in Shylock’s account of the patriarchs.

entities.name: Jesus
entities.body: Jesus of Nazareth, referred to in Shylock’s account of the possessed swine.

entities.name: Hagar
entities.body: The biblical woman whose descendants Shylock invokes in his insult to Launcelet.

entities.name: Daniel
entities.body: The biblical figure famed for wise judgment, invoked as a comparison in court.

entities.name: Barabbas
entities.body: The prisoner released instead of Jesus in the Gospel account.

entities.name: Janus
entities.body: The Roman god traditionally represented with two faces.

entities.name: Nestor
entities.body: The aged Greek king renowned for wisdom in the Trojan stories.

entities.name: Jason
entities.body: The Greek hero who sought the Golden Fleece, used as a comparison for the suitors.

entities.name: The Sibyl
entities.body: The long-lived prophetess of classical legend.

entities.name: Diana
entities.body: The goddess associated with chastity and the moon.

entities.name: Hercules
entities.body: The classical hero also called Alcides.

entities.name: Lichas
entities.body: Hercules’s servant in classical myth.

entities.name: Fortune
entities.body: The personified power governing luck and changes of worldly circumstances.

entities.name: The Fates
entities.body: The three supernatural sisters governing human destiny.

entities.name: Venus
entities.body: The goddess of love.

entities.name: Cupid
entities.body: The god of love.

entities.name: Hesione
entities.body: The Trojan princess offered to a sea monster and rescued by Hercules in the comparison.

entities.name: Mars
entities.body: The Roman god of war.

entities.name: Midas
entities.body: The mythical king whose touch turned things to gold.

entities.name: Scylla
entities.body: The sea monster paired with Charybdis as an image of unavoidable danger.

entities.name: Charybdis
entities.body: The monstrous whirlpool paired with Scylla in classical myth.

entities.name: Troilus
entities.body: The Trojan lover of Cressida.

entities.name: Cressida
entities.body: Troilus’s beloved, called Cressid here.

entities.name: Thisbe
entities.body: The lover of Pyramus in the classical story.

entities.name: Dido
entities.body: The queen of Carthage who loved Aeneas.

entities.name: Medea
entities.body: The sorceress associated with Jason, invoked for her rejuvenating magic.

entities.name: Aeson
entities.body: Jason’s father, restored to youth by Medea in the myth.

entities.name: Orpheus
entities.body: The mythical musician whose music could move animals, trees and stones.

entities.name: Endymion
entities.body: The beautiful sleeper loved by the moon goddess in classical myth.

entities.name: Argus
entities.body: The many-eyed watcher of classical myth.

entities.name: God
entities.body: The deity invoked in the characters’ prayers and oaths.

entities.name: The devil
entities.body: The supernatural tempter invoked in religious references and curses.
